faq.a: Salah is associated with the Arabic form صَلَاح, whose core sense is salah; righteousness, goodness.

faq.q: What is the origin of Salah?
faq.a: Salah is associated with Arabic. Salah is Arabic صَلَاح (Ṣalāḥ), meaning 'righteousness, goodness'. It is distinct from صَلَاة (ṣalāh, ritual prayer).
Yes — the underlying form صَلَاح is Arabic.
Salah can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Salah should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. The root ص ل ح is Quranic, but Ṣalāḥ is not itself a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Salah mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Salah is rendered صلاح and carries the sense صلاح، نیکی.

faq.q: What does Salah mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Salah is rendered صلاح and carries the sense صلاح، نیکی.
A romanized syllable approximation is sa-lah. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Salah?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Salah, salah. Script forms are صلاح, صَلَاح, सलाह.

faq.q: Is Salah a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
